title: Yellowmoon camera registry
description: data/cameras/registry.json, generated by training/sensor_map/build_registry.py from the table in docs/03. Lookup: exact model ID -> sensor family -> default. A model ID that is not in 'bodies' gets 'default_profile' with match 'default'. Also required (checked by training/sensor_map/validate_profiles.py): model IDs and model strings unique, every profile id has a profile file, every profile has exactly one 'exact' body, 'via' names the profile's measured body for 'sensor_family' and is null otherwise, every 'default' body uses default_profile, model_strings agree with bodies, the sensor fields come together and the pixel pitch they give is within 0.5 to 20 micrometres, and the white scale (docs/03): [r, 1, b] with positive r and b, exactly [1, 1, 1] for an 'exact' or 'sensor_family' body and for a 'default' body whose source kind is 'none', and a source that says how it was found.

default_profile.description: Profile for every Sony body without an entry (the A7R IV stand-in).

sensors.description: Where the sensor geometry of the bodies comes from and how it was read.

profiles.description: Profile ids and their files, relative to data/cameras/.

model.description: IFD0 Model string, as ExifTool names the ID.

body.description: Display name, for example 'Sony A7R IV'.

via.description: For sensor_family: display name of the profile's measured body. Null otherwise.

white_scale.description: [r, 1, b]: the factor that takes the body's raw white to the white of its profile's curves, w_profile = w_body * white_scale (docs/03, White scale of stand-in bodies). Applied to the as-shot white, Pick white and the illuminant estimator's input, and folded into the initial gains of the raw stages. Exactly [1, 1, 1] for a body whose profile was measured on it or on its sensor.

white_scale_source.description: Where the white scale comes from: the kind, the files whose presets it was fitted on, the residuals of the fit against both references, and a note.

kind.description: 'own_curves': the profile was measured on this body. 'same_sensor': the body shares the measured body's sensor. 'presets': fitted on the white-balance presets stored in the body's own files. 'sibling': taken from another body whose published colour matrix is the same. 'none': nothing was measured; the whites are not corrected.

files.description: The files the presets were read from (names only), for kind 'presets'; empty otherwise.

residual.description: For kind 'presets': the fit against the presets and the cross-check with the body's published colour matrix at D65. Angles are between the preset's white and the locus white at its label, degrees, averaged over the five Kelvin presets; daylight_k is the colour temperature the profile's locus reads for the Daylight preset.

matrix_scale.description: The scale the published colour matrix at D65 would give: [r, 1, b].

sensor_width_mm.description: Width of the full sensor in millimetres, from the maker's published specification. With active_width_px it gives the pixel pitch 1000 * sensor_width_mm / active_width_px (docs/algorithms/03-diffraction-deconvolution.md section 2.2). A crop mode does not change it.

active_width_px.description: Width in pixels of the largest 3:2 still image recorded from the full sensor (the horizontal count of the effective pixels).

pixel_pitch_um.description: Optional. The pixel pitch in micrometres when the maker states it; it overrides the value computed from sensor_width_mm and active_width_px.

sensor_source_kind.description: 'maker': read from an excerpt of the maker's specification page. 'restated': the maker's specification as restated by a retailer or reference site (the maker's page was not seen).

sensor_source.description: The pages the sensor fields were read from and how (the source of every value is recorded in its entry).

model_strings.description: Model string -> model ID, for files whose maker note has no usable 0xB001 (docs/03: when they disagree the model ID wins).
